Confirmed the five property definition bullets and the PR Body Template block are untouched (only prose above them and the section bodies changed), matching the body's claim.

## PR Self-Check Result

### Fix
None.

### Note
- [Grounded/Decidable] The claim "`pr-selfcheck/SKILL.md`'s hard-wrap parser stops matching nested list items, which it would otherwise flag throughout every body now that nesting is the required shape" is only partially realized by the diff. Only violation-rule 2 (indented continuation line after a list item) was updated to exempt lines that themselves start with a list marker. Violation-rule 1 ("two or more consecutive non-empty lines with no blank line between them, where neither line begins with a block marker") and the block-marker definition itself were left untouched, and that definition literally says "a line starting with" `-`/`*`/`+`/etc. Read at face value (marker checked at column 0, before stripping indentation), two stacked 2-space-indented sub-bullets with no blank line between them — the exact style this PR now mandates, and the style used throughout this very PR body and the reformatted `pr-guidelines.md` — would still match rule 1 as a false-positive hard-wrap violation. Read with indentation stripped first (the natural way an LLM executing this natural-language spec would apply it), there is no false positive: I ran both interpretations against this PR's own body — the strict column-0 reading found 5 "violations," the indentation-stripped reading found 0. Since `pr-selfcheck` is executed by an LLM doing reading comprehension rather than a literal regex engine, the loose reading is the one that will actually run, so this is unlikely to cause real misfires — flagged as a Note rather than a Fix because it turns on how an ambiguous natural-language rule gets read, not on a settled contradiction.

### Unverifiable
- [Grounded] "Clause mapping built against `git show main:claude/skills/git-workflow/pr-guidelines.md`, covering the 37 rule bullets the reformat carried over" — the record lives at `ikuwowfiles/pr-guidelines-reformat-check.md`, which the body itself notes is gitignored and not checkable from a clone. The body already discloses this limitation.

### Property walk
- Decidable: purpose, decision shape, and inverted pyramid are present; every top-level bullet in both the body and the reformatted file carries its own claim, with supporting material nested beneath, consistent with the new rule the PR itself adds.
- Grounded: verified derivable claims hold — `git show b9256e4:claude/skills/git-workflow/pr-guidelines.md` (the merge base) has exactly 45 top-level `- ` bullets and 0 nested ones, the largest flat list among the 17 markdown files under `claude/rules/` and `claude/skills/` at that commit, matching the body's count exactly; the five property-definition bullets and the PR Body Template block are byte-identical to the merge base, matching the body's "untouched" claim.
- Necessary: no diff paraphrase, no restated facts, no file/line-count enumeration; each Key changes bullet states a distinct decision.
- Scoped: all three changed files (`git-workflow/SKILL.md`, `pr-guidelines.md`, `pr-selfcheck/SKILL.md`) map onto a Key changes bullet — the `git-workflow/SKILL.md` one-line severity-wording change is covered by "goes with them" in the severity bullet.
- Conformant: title is one line and accurate, no auto-close keywords, checkboxes used correctly (all `- [x]`, all author-verified), and no hard-wrap violations found in the body under either block-marker interpretation used above (the ambiguity discussed in Note affects the *skill's own future runs*, not this body's formatting).

### Verdict
PASS

tool_input.command:
cd /Users/ikuwow/dotfiles
git ls-tree -r --name-only main -- claude/rules claude/skills | grep '\.md$' | wc -l
echo "---files---"
git ls-tree -r --name-only main -- claude/rules claude/skills | grep '\.md$'

cd /Users/ikuwow/dotfiles
for f in $(git ls-tree -r --name-only main -- claude/rules claude/skills | grep '\.md$'); do
  top=$(git show main:"$f" | grep -c '^- ')
  nested=$(git show main:"$f" | grep -c '^ \+- ')
  echo "$top $nested $f"
done | sort -rn
git -C /Users/ikuwow/dotfiles show b9256e4:claude/skills/git-workflow/pr-guidelines.md | sed -n '/^- Decidable/,/^## Decidable/p' | head -20
